text.p: China's trade surplus expanded to nearly $3.0 billion in August with exports showing their second successive monthly increase after several months of declines, according to customs figures released Saturday.
Exports in August totalled $14.1 billion with imports at about $11.1 billion, for a surplus of about $2.99 billion, said the figures released by the Customs Administration.
That compared with exports of $12.53 billion in August of 1995, and imports of $11.59 billion in the year-ago month when the monthly trade surplus was $940 million.
China's trade surplus for the first eight months of this year was $4.99 billion as exports slid 4.2 percent year-on-year to $90.61 billion and imports rose 7.9 percent to $85.62 billion.

That was still sharply down the trade surplus in the first eight months of last year of $15.27 billion, which had been fuelled by a stampede by exporters to win orders before a cut in government-paid export rebates.
Exports slumped in the first six months of 1996, pinched by rising wages and the relative strength of the currency, the renminbi.
